name: Pane
text: Dark themes don’t just strain eyes—they bury errors in shadows and mute critical signals. A one-click toggle to light mode still hides the real trade-off: users won’t notice mislabeled data or misaligned graphs until it’s too late. Instead, default to a high-contrast light theme with a *subtle* dark mode option—visibility first, then preference. Settle it with A/B tests measuring error detection rates, not just glare complaints.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A high-contrast light theme solves glare but ignores the real risk: users in dim rooms will squint at white glare while missing errors buried in bright noise. The better alternative is a *balanced* theme—dark UI with high-contrast elements (bold colors, sharp borders) that keeps errors visible without sacrificing readability. Settle it with a user test: measure error detection speed in both dark and bright rooms.
